text:
Ben H: heads-up, CI just started failing on the eu-gpu onboarding job. terraform apply is erroring with a state lock that never clears. logs attached in the job but snippet below:

Ben H: ```
Error: Error locking state: Error acquiring the state lock: ConditionalCheckFailedException: The conditional request failed
	status code: 400, request id: 9b2f-...
```

Alice K: ugh, same symptom as the workspace rename we did last week? did the gitops job run a state move? :thinking_face:

Maya R: I saw the pipeline attempt a `workspace rename -> import` flow at 03:12UTC. It did `terraform state mv` between keys and then the GitOps apply retried while the DynamoDB lock record still had the old key metadata.

Priya (oncall): links? which repo/job? I can jump in and force-unlock if needed but want to avoid stomping a live apply.

Ben H: job: ci/gpu-provision/eu-onboard (link: https://ci.internal/runs/8923) main error was during `apply` after `plan`. The CI log shows the state lock created (key: infra/tfstate/eu/gpu-pools.tfstate), then a subsequent reconcile created a new key (infra/tfstate/eu/gpu-pools-v2.tfstate) and the operator tried to move state. Dynamo record now references the old key but the S3 blob lease still exists.

infra-bot: deploybot: detected 3 concurrent applies against workspace "eu-gpu-pools" in last 10m :warning:

Alice K: do NOT force-unlock blindly. If state mv partially succeeded we could have the same resource in both states and a force-unlock will let another apply overwrite the intended mapping.

Maya R: quick triage steps I did: checked dynamodb lock table, saw lock id `lock-197123...` with expiration 5m but TTL not expiring (Dynamo TTL delayed). I also ran `aws s3api head-object` on both keys and saw the v2 key exists but with a different ETag.

Ben H: tried `terraform force-unlock -force lock-197123...` locally but stopped after noticing the CI runner PID was 2941 and a `terraform apply` container still existed in k8s. Rolled it back.

Priya (oncall): good call. ops checklist: 1) find any running apply tasks, 2) confirm which state file is authoritative, 3) run safe recovery. I'm free in 20m to coordinate a brief mitigation window.

Ops SRE: +1. We should snapshot both state files first. command: `aws s3 cp s3://redwood-tfstate/infra/tfstate/eu/gpu-pools.tfstate ./snapshots/gpu-old.json` and same for v2. Also export the dynamo lock item: `aws dynamodb get-item --table-name tfstate-locks --key '{"LockID":{"S":"infra/tfstate/eu/gpu-pools.tfstate"}}' > ./snapshots/lock-old.json`

Alice K: propose fallback plan: 1) snapshot s3 + dynamo, 2) run `terraform state list` against both workspaces (using `TF_STATE` env trick) to confirm dupes, 3) if duplicates, run `terraform state rm` on the stale copy and then `terraform import` into the authoritative one.

Maya R: another important fix: update the gitops pipeline to pause new applies while a state-move run is ongoing. We should add a lock-check step that queries the dynamo table and refuses a run if a lock exists older than X. I'll open a PR for the pipeline: gitlab.com/redwood/infra-ci/-/merge_requests/106 (draft).

Ben H: for the immediate incident, Priya can you coordinate with SRE to cordon the CI runner namespace and we can snapshot then attempt a controlled force-unlock + run of `terraform plan` with `-refresh=false` to avoid surprises?

Priya (oncall): yes, I'll cordon the namespace in 10m and put a notice in #eng-infra. Also will create a short downtime window 2026-03-18 04:10-04:25 UTC to run recovery.

infra-bot: incidentbot: created incident INC-2026-0318-12 (priority P2) and paged Ops SRE.

Ops SRE: after snapshot, we can run a staged recovery: restore s3 snapshot to a temp key `infra/tfstate/eu/gpu-pools-recovery.tfstate`, run `terraform state pull` against the temp key, compare resource lists, then perform a deliberate `state mv` for conflicting resources. If all good, switch the repo to point at the recovery key and re-run apply.

Alice K: one more long-term item: we need to standardize state-key naming during workspace renames (use immutable keys + alias mapping metadata) to avoid blob-lease churn. I'll add to the infra backlog and tag for next sprint.

Ben H: thanks team. I'll wait for the cordon + snapshots, then Priya ping me and I'll run the recovery steps with Ops SRE. Leaving the job muted for now. :thumbsup:

Maya R: logging the runbook steps in the incident ticket (INC-2026-0318-12) so we have an audit trail.

Priya (oncall): done the cordon, snapshots started, pinging when complete.

Ben H: final note: adding a pre-check to GitOps to refuse automated state moves without a human ack would have prevented this. Please include that in the PR, Maya.

Maya R: will do. PR will include a flag `require_human_ack: true` for any run that touches `tfstate/*-rename*` paths.

Ops SRE: once this is resolved let's also run a chronic-job to validate Dynamo TTL behavior across accounts (we're seeing delayed expiries during heavy write bursts).

Ben H: agreed. thanks everyone, staying on call until recovery done. :coffee:
